lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Marcio Ferreira Santos | Lesson 8 -- Say Exactly Which One

listenings.text: Thanks for making time. Let me describe the role, because the title on the advertisement does not tell the whole story. We are looking for someone who can own pricing across eight countries, not someone who runs a team of analysts. The person we hire will report to the chief commercial officer, and the mandate is to build a model that works at SKU level in markets which are very different from each other. The candidate we want has done this at least once before, in a business where price is the main lever. One more thing. The role, which is new, does not exist in any other company in the group. So the first six months are about defining the scope, not delivering a number.

Quick debrief on the two candidates we saw this morning. The first one, who came from a consultancy, gave the cleaner presentation. He described a framework which is well known, and he described it very well. The second candidate was harder to follow, but he talked about a model that he actually built himself, in a business where the data was terrible. And when I asked him what he would do differently, he answered without defending himself. For me that is the difference. The person we need is not the one who explains a framework best. It is the one who has lived the problem the framework is trying to solve.

extra_audio.text: First, the company writes the specification that describes the role. Then it agrees the criteria which candidates have to meet. After that, the recruiter contacts the people who match the profile. Next, the panel interviews the candidates that reached the final stage. Finally, the team runs the due diligence before the offer is signed.

paras: This document describes a role that does not exist yet in the group. It is written for candidates who have already owned pricing in a large retail business, and for the internal panel that will run the interviews.

The person we appoint will own pricing across eight countries. The mandate, which was approved by the board in March, is to build a model that works at SKU level in markets which are structurally different from each other. The first deliverable is not a number: it is the specification that defines the scope of the model.

The criteria are three. First, a candidate who has built a pricing model, not only used one. Second, evidence of work in a business where price is the main commercial lever. Third, the ability to lead a cross-functional team that includes analysts, category managers and finance.

Two notes. The proprietary data that the group already collects is a strong asset, and it is under-used. And the due diligence, which is standard for every executive appointment, will include two references from people who reported to the candidate, not only to people the candidate reported to.

gist.prompt: Read once for the main idea. What is this document really looking for?
choices: Someone who can explain a pricing framework very well
Someone who has built a pricing model and led people across functions
Someone who will deliver a revenue number in the first six months
